We've worked with 130 life science companies, preclinical through phase 3, to deploy AI securely inside the systems they already work in.

Pharma runs on decades of closed software like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS. None of it has an AI layer or speaks MCP, so agents cannot reach the systems where the work lives.

Enjamb is that layer. Our agents run on top of existing systems and data, with no migration, and they reach the lab systems and internal tools no other AI touches. They learn how a team works, then do the work in Slack, in Teams, and in the systems themselves, across preclinical research, clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.

This is AI tailored for how medicine gets made.
long_description.after:
General models know a lot. Experts know when something is wrong before they can say why, and they earned that over years of getting it wrong. Outside of code, the record of how they got good sits locked inside the companies where they did the work, on old servers, in formats nobody reads anymore, sometimes on paper.

Enjamb builds Earned Intelligence. We recover that expert work and use it to give foundation models the intuition they can't learn from the open web. For companies, we train custom models on their own history and deploy agents that work alongside their teams.

We work with 13 AI and robotics labs, building the data, environments and evals that give their models intuition for the physical world.

one_liner.after: Earned Intelligence. Data, RL environments and custom models

long_description.before:
Egoist Machines is building infrastructure for a world where your personal context belongs to you, rather than to the apps and AI companies you use. Today, every assistant and consumer app builds its own version of you. We think that architecture is backwards. Your context should live with you, persist across products, and be available to any model, app or agent you choose.

AI Passport is the first layer of that infrastructure. It brings the context you generate across AI assistants and everyday apps into one portable profile you control. Tell ChatGPT something and Claude can already know it, for example. Switch to a new product and it can understand you from the first interaction, without the new company needing to own the underlying data.

Apps integrate through Sign in with AI Passport, requesting only the context they need for a specific purpose and duration. Users can see what is being accessed and revoke that access later. Underneath, we have built our own memory infrastructure for fast, compact per-user retrieval and permissioned access.

We are distributing AI Passport directly to consumers through first-party products, while integrating it into consumer applications with existing distribution. Every new product that uses Passport gives users another reason to maintain their context there, and every additional Passport holder makes the context layer more useful to developers.

The next step is to build a true Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents. We call it Digital Domovoy, the hardware extension of AI Passport. Instead of your most personal context ultimately living on somebody else's servers, it lives and is processed locally on hardware you control. AI Passport becomes the permission layer between that private local context and the cloud models and internet services you choose to use.

Our North Star is the Egoist Machine: an intelligent system whose memory, incentives and actions are governed by the individual it represents.
long_description.after:
The race is on for every AI company to capture and monetize your data. We believe it should be the other way round. At Egoist Machines (https://ego.ist) we are building the layer that gives you control over your own context, and the ability to bring it with you to any AI model, app or agent. Our first product in this stack is Ink (https://ink.ego.ist).

Ink takes drafts written by ChatGPT or Claude and edits them into something you can send without altering facts, names, numbers or quotes. A proprietary SotA writing model powers the engine.

AI Passport is the first layer of the Egoist stack and it is what lets Ink work. It lets you combine context generated by you on AI assistants and normal apps into a portable profile that you own and control. Ink uses AI Passport to learn your voice from writing you already have. If you tell ChatGPT something, Claude knows it too. Apps can access Passport through the 'Sign in with AI Passport' protocol. They can ask for only specific contexts that they need, for a specific purpose and time and you can see and remove that access at any time. AI Passport uses our own memory infrastructure to give fast compact memory retrieval for each user.

Each product we make on top of Passport provides people with more utility and thus more reasons to keep their context on Passport. And the more people have Passport, the more valuable it becomes to developers who build on top of it. This is how a writing tool will grow into the context layer for all of AI.

Our North Star is the Egoist Machine. An intelligent system that holds your memory, pursues your interests and acts on your behalf.

one_liner.before: Your personal context, securely portable across every AI app.
one_liner.after: Own your AI context. Ink, our first app, makes drafts sound like you

That understanding powers three ways to get work done:

Sidekick: click your Mac’s notch and say “finish this for me.” It already has your context and gets to work across your apps and browser with its own cursor, while you keep working.

Proactive intelligence: wake up to work already prepared. The reply you forgot, drafted. The subscription renewing tomorrow, caught. The report you promised, ready for review. Sentient waits for your approval before acting.

long_description.before:
**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.
long_description.after:
boat gives AI agents powerful, affordable cloud computers. Spawn full Ubuntu VMs with a browser, desktop, persistent files, Docker and the tools to do real work, without managing the entire infrastructure yourself.

As agents tackle harder problems in engineering, math and science, they need more than inference: they need computers to run experiments, execute code and verify their work. We believe access to enough powerful, permissive, inexpensive computers will be the next AI bottleneck.

We first built boat for ourselves while working on cloud coding agents, then opened it up to other builders. Our approach is product-first: make it easy for agents to experiment, build and scale.

Run agents inside a VM or prompt, observe and wrap them from outside through the CLI, API or SDKs. Run Docker, systemd, databases and cron; open web apps, games, 3D scenes and IDEs; stop, resume and fork VMs.

https://boat.dev
https://docs.boat.dev

We're starting with asset-backed lending and revenue-based financing, using a company's own operating data to make decisions quickly. Our vision is to become the financial rails for the machine economy.

We've done this before with real assets. Artem Milinchuk founded FarmTogether (YC W'18 accepted), a farmland investment platform he scaled to $220M in assets across 50 farms, and previously invested at Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan and was CFO at Full Harvest. long_description.before:
Organizely helps American manufacturers use AI to lower production costs. 

Factories depend on three resources: materials, equipment, and labor. Costs rise unexpectedly when components are missing, machines go down, or staffing doesn’t match demand. We experienced this firsthand while owning and operating a factory in the U.S. for six years. As we scaled, it was expensive to resolve factory-wide bottlenecks quickly and it became harder to stay competitive on price. 

Other companies are trying to layer AI agents on top of legacy ERPs to do logistics work, but the underlying data architectures limit how much those agents can understand and do. So we’re building a new ERP from the ground up for the era of AI. 

Organizely is an AI-native ERP with AI reasoning and machine learning algorithms embedded throughout for a single intelligent platform that can model, predict, and act. We natively automate all core manufacturing workflows including demand planning, raw material tracking, machine maintenance, and production scheduling. 

Organizely continuously improves over time, suggesting new ways for manufacturers to reduce costs and produce more with their existing facilities and teams. It's the whole factory solved. 

We’ve deployed to factories across six U.S. states and now we’re bringing AI to all factories across America. 🇺🇸

long_description.before:
Canos is bringing a human-grade liquid biopsy platform for dogs, starting with a single blood draw. We sequence cell-free DNA to perform multi-modal analysis of fragmentation, copy number variation, native methylation (5mC and 5hmC) and more to detect cancer signals. Owners bank a healthy baseline for their dog and track changes every year. Dogs already diagnosed get personalized monitoring through treatment. We partner with mobile vets and vet clinics to serve SF and NYC. 

Our mission is to make pet cancer curable through early detection and monitoring.
long_description.after:
There are 3 times more dog cancer patients than human cancer patients diagnosed in the US every year. Canos is bringing a human-grade liquid biopsy platform for dogs, starting with a single blood draw. Cancer changes how DNA breaks apart and the methylation patterns. We sequence the fragments in a routine blood draw and use AI to spot those changes across the genome. A suspicious result can prompt a vet to order imaging. Early detections save lives and reduce cancer treatment costs. After diagnosis, repeat draws show whether the cancer signal is rising or falling between scans.

Our AI-empowered bioinformatics model reached 91% sensitivity at 95% specificity. We’re two Oxford scientists who previously built an AI pathology system at ZYTCA that reached over 10,000 veterinary clinics in China.

We estimate a $4 billion annual US screening opportunity at one $200 test a year for 20 million dogs in higher-income households. By following the same dogs through diagnosis and treatment, we’re building a dataset to learn which changes in blood predict relapse in cancers that dogs and people share.

Our mission is to make pet cancer curable.

We started off building the highest performance, 470 volt electric off-road vehicles but we realized our ultra power dense battery packs are useful for mobile and stationary energy storage and power export, for military and consumer use cases. We develop battery packs, power electronics, and traction powertrain systems for vehicles.

For the majority of 2026 we were marketing our electric off-road vehicles, but we pivoted to selling our high performance battery packs and power export capabilities in the month of September. We went from having $769,000 in consumer pre-orders (possibly low conversion rate to sales) to $421,815 in realized revenue in 1 month, with a $792,000 qualified pipeline. 

Our tech is so compelling because the safety and layout of high voltage battery packs has only been mastered by large, well funded OEM companies who have brought it in-house. That means all other companies without the in-house expertise rely on battery companies to develop packs, and power electronics companies to develop power export capabilities. SPM has both of those capabilities in-house so we can ensure a fast turnaround and much more reliable product. 

One of the biggest priorities of the department of war is energy dominance. We're seeing it constantly in new solicitations. Our strategy is superior - become a prime, but simultaneously service primes because most of then don't actually have the battery and power electronics expertise we have.

Founded by Jon Powers - Ex-Tesla Sr. Mechanical Integration Engineer leading Cybertruck vehicle integration.
